sense: at liberty, not a slave or a prisoner

terms.grammar: adjective; “free from” with ab or the ablative
evidence: Phaedr. 3.7.27: rēgnāre nōlō, līber ut nōn sim mihi
terms.comment: Free as against a slave or a prisoner, and free from something: ab arbitrīs lībera, free from onlookers. Free time is tempus līberum (Traupman 52) or ōtium. To be free to do something is licet (licet mihi, I may). Not “costing nothing”: that is grātīs (see free, costing nothing).

phrases.latin: age, sī quō abīre est animus, est licentia? — nōn plānē est, inquit. — fruere quae laudās, canis: rēgnāre nōlō, līber ut nōn sim mihi
phrases.english: ‘Well, if you want to go somewhere, are you allowed?’ ‘Not really,’ he said. ‘Enjoy what you praise, dog: I don’t want to be a king if I can’t be free.’

phrases.latin: quoūsque calceī nusquam, toga fēriāta, līber tōtus diēs?
phrases.english: how long will it be no shoes, your toga on holiday, the whole day free?

sources: Lewis & Short: liber
